Suggest assembling full content first then applying renderInline/stripMdFull, OR de-duplicating consecutive identical line fragments before rendering.
(Pre-existing) Silence Recharts width(-1)/height(-1) warning by guarding ResponsiveContainer with explicit minWidth/minHeight.
critical_code_review_comments: AIChat.jsx renderInline (line 417) applies regex replacements on every streaming token — when a chunk boundary lands inside **bold** markers, the same content can be rendered twice during partial-stream phases and survives in the final state. Consider buffering until newline boundary or de-duplicating before commit.

AIChat.jsx PlanSnapshot (line 435) cleanly captures latest user+assistant pair only — correct architectural choice for the user's snapshot complaint. Off-screen container at position:fixed left:-10000 (line 292) renders independently of the modal panel, so html2canvas captures full layout regardless of panel scroll. Verified working.

AI streaming duplication bug is cosmetic and PRE-EXISTING (visible in PNG too) — not a regression.
rca of the issue: AI streaming text duplication RCA: AIChat.jsx renderInline (line 417-428) runs regex `replace(/\*\*(.+?)\*\*/g, ...)` on every state update as tokens stream in. When a chunk lands mid-token (e.g. just `**Bilkul sahi soch rahe hain aap!**`) and the next chunk repeats a similar prefix (LLM SSE quirk or React state batching), both fragments can be appended into the message buffer. Result: visible duplicate sentences. The snapshot PNG inherits these duplicates via stripMdFull which only strips markdown but does not de-duplicate. Mitigation: in handleStream, before setMessages, run a regex like content.replace(/^(.{20,})\n\1/gm,'$1') to collapse immediate exact-line repeats, OR change SSE buffering to commit only complete sentences.
